forces: Flute, oboe (cor anglais), clarinet, horn and bassoon
performers: Wind Quintet of the Royal Orchestra, Copenhagen (Det Kgl. Kapels Blæserkvintet): Holger Gilbert-Jespersen, flute; Svend Christian Felumb, oboe and cor anglais; Aage Oxenvad, clarinet; Hans Sørensen, horn; Knud Lassen, bassoon
intro: The last movement of Nielsen’s Wind Quintet is a Prelude for cor anglais and flute followed by a theme and eleven variations on his hymn tune Min Jesus, lad mit Hjerte faa. Four of these five players had given the first public performance in 1922; this recording was made in Copenhagen in January 1936.

sections.label: Intro · Prelude, cor anglais and flute
Theme · Hymn tune in A major, five parts
sections.mNote: A sixteen-bar chorale with the flute on top.

sections.label: Var 2 · Flute runs, short staccato notes
Var 4 · Più vivo, all five together
Var 8 · Poco meno, low pedal notes
Coda · Andantino festivo, theme in A major
sections.mNote: The hymn tune returns in chords, pp rising to ff.

cues.title: Prelude, Adagio
cues.text: The Prelude is marked Adagio. Cor anglais, horn and bassoon sound a fortissimo chord marked pesante, the clarinet joins in the third bar and the flute enters in the fourth. The oboist plays cor anglais from here to the end of the theme at bar 42.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. 129–132: bars 1–4, the staff heading “Corno inglese (Oboe)”, and “muta in ob.” at the end of the theme.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Flute alone
cues.text: The flute plays alone in long runs of triplets, marked accel. and then rall. Horn and bassoon return at pianissimo in bar 8, clarinet and bassoon play more pianissimo triplets in bar 9, and bar 10 ends on fermatas.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, p. 129, bars 4–10.

cues.title: Poco agitato, bar 11
cues.text: Bar 11 is marked poco agitato. The cor anglais plays a melody in triplets at fortissimo while clarinet, horn and bassoon repeat accented chords, also in triplets. The flute rests until bar 16.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, p. 130, bars 11–16.

cues.title: Felumb and the cor anglais
cues.text: According to Torben Meyer, Nielsen heard Svend Christian Felumb practising a cor anglais solo from Berlioz’s Symphonie fantastique behind the scenes at a concert. That night he telephoned Felumb to ask whether a player could change instruments within a movement, and is said to have composed this Prelude at once.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11 (2003), preface to the Quintet: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, p. xxxvii, retelling Torben Meyer and Frede Schandorf Petersen, Carl Nielsen. Kunstneren og Mennesket (1947–48), vol. 2, pp. 214–215.

cues.title: Theme, the hymn tune
cues.text: After a pause marked lunga the theme begins in A major, Un poco andantino, in 3/4. It is the tune of Nielsen’s hymn Min Jesus, lad mit Hjerte faa, set in five parts with the flute on top at p. It runs for sixteen bars, 27 to 42, and ends on a fermata.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. 131–132: “lunga” at bar 26, and bars 27–42. The hymn tune as the theme of the variations: Catalogue of Carl Nielsen’s Works, CNW 70 and CNW 184, https://www.kb.dk/dcm/cnw/document.xq?n=70 and https://www.kb.dk/dcm/cnw/document.xq?n=184

cues.title: Variation 1, horn and bassoon
cues.text: In the first variation, bars 43 to 58, flute, oboe and clarinet rest. Horn and bassoon play a duet at forte, and the variation ends on a fermata for all five.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, p. 133, bars 43–58.

cues.title: Variation 2, Un poco di più
cues.text: The flute plays runs of sixteenth notes above short staccato notes in clarinet and horn. In bar 68 flute, oboe, clarinet and bassoon repeat sixteenth notes together, marked fz and falling to p.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. 134–135, bars 59–74.

cues.title: Variation 3, Meno mosso
cues.text: The oboe has the melody at mp, marked espressivo, over a low horn at pp and bassoon at p. The clarinet and flute join later, and the variation ends at bar 90 on a ppp chord with fermatas, marked rall.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. 135–136, bars 75–90.

cues.title: Variation 4, Più vivo
cues.text: All five instruments begin together at fortissimo with repeated staccato notes, and triplets appear from bar 93. The variation ends at bar 106 with short accented notes in clarinet, horn and bassoon marked ffz, and a fermata on the last rest.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. 136–137, bars 91–106.

cues.title: Variation 5, clarinet and bassoon
cues.text: Tempo giusto. Flute, oboe and horn rest while clarinet and bassoon play a duet. The bassoon plays short bursts of repeated sixteenth notes and the clarinet plays runs, with a long trill in bar 118.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. 138–140, bars 107–122.

cues.title: Variation 6, Andantino con moto
cues.text: Flute, clarinet and bassoon start together at p, and oboe and horn join a few bars later. The variation ends at bar 138 with a diminuendo and fermatas, marked rall.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, p. 140, bars 123–138.

cues.title: Variation 7, bassoon alone
cues.text: The bassoon plays alone for sixteen bars, 139 to 154, in flowing triplets that begin at mf. Bar 154 is a fermata for all five, marked lunga.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. 141–142, bars 139–154.

cues.title: Recording, January 1936
cues.text: The Wind Quintet of the Royal Orchestra recorded the work for HMV in Copenhagen in January 1936; the Menuet side was re-made in May. The seven sides, with the Taagen letter from Nielsen’s music for Moderen on an eighth, were issued as the four records DB 5200–5203.
cues.evidence: Labels of HMV DB 5200 to DB 5203 and the transferor’s description: Internet Archive item db-5200-3-nielsen-wind-quintet-iii (description and label scans of HMV DB 5200 and DB 5203), https://archive.org/details/db-5200-3-nielsen-wind-quintet-iii. Matrices and recording dates: The Gramophone Company Discography (after Alan Kelly), matrices 2CS 291–297 and 318, https://www.gramophonecompanydiscography.com/.

cues.title: Variation 8, Poco meno
cues.text: The oboe plays the melody at mp and the clarinet answers with marcato figures, while horn and bassoon hold low notes tied across the bars. The flute joins later.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. 142–143, bars 155–170.

cues.title: The set in America, 1937
cues.text: In August 1937 the Philadelphia dealer H. Royer Smith listed the four records in its bulletin The New Records at $2.50 each. The reviewer found the quintet “at once old-fashioned and modern”.
cues.evidence: The New Records, vol. 5 no. 6 (H. Royer Smith Company, Philadelphia, August 1937), entry for Nielsen’s Quintet for Wind Instruments, Op. 43, DB5200 to DB5203: https://archive.org/details/TNR05

cues.title: Variation 9, horn alone
cues.text: The horn plays alone from bar 171, Tempo giusto. Its phrases fade to ppp before the pauses marked lunga in bars 174 and 178 and resume at ff. The last phrase ends at pppp in bar 186 on a fermata marked molto lunga.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. 143–144, bars 171–186.

cues.title: Nielsen on the horn variation
cues.text: Nielsen told the horn player Hans Sørensen that he imagined him standing on a hill and blowing so that it could be heard in every nook and cranny. Under the horn part in the draft he wrote that without great naive devotion to the mood of nature it would not work.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11 (2003), preface to the Quintet: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. xxxvi–xxxvii, quoting Nielsen’s remark to Sørensen as given by Torben Meyer, and the note under the horn part in the draft (our translations of the Danish).

cues.title: Variation 10, Allegretto
cues.text: The metre is 6/8 and the flute begins alone at mp. The variation lasts thirty-two bars, 187 to 218, twice as long as those before it, and ends with a crescendo to ff, a diminuendo and a rall. to a p chord on a fermata.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. 144–145, bars 187–218.

cues.title: Variation 11, Tempo di marcia
cues.text: Tempo di marcia, in 4/4. Clarinet, oboe and bassoon play trills marked fz, with short figures in horn and flute. The tempo quickens at bar 235 (più mosso), and a crescendo, rall. and diminuendo fill bars 243 to 247.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, pp. 146–148, bars 219–247.

cues.title: Andantino festivo, bar 248
cues.text: The hymn tune returns in chords for all five instruments, marked pp and poco a poco cresc. The last chord, in bar 265, is fortissimo under a fermata. In a programme note Nielsen wrote that the variations end with the theme “in all its simplicity”.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11, Chamber Music 2 (Edition Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, 2003), Quintet, Op. 43, third movement, with the bar numbers printed there: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, p. 149, bars 248–265. Programme note to Emil Holm (undated), quoted in Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11 (2003), preface to the Quintet: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, p. xxxvii (our translation of “i al sin Enkelhed”).

cues.title: Nielsen’s funeral, 9 October 1931
cues.text: The first hymn sung at Nielsen’s funeral on 9 October 1931 was Min Jesus, lad mit Hjerte faa. The wind quintet of the Royal Orchestra played this Andantino festivo at the grave in Vestre Kirkegård as the coffin was lowered.
cues.evidence: Carl Nielsen Edition, series II, vol. 11 (2003), preface to the Quintet: https://www.kb.dk/dcm/assets/cnu/pdf/CNU_II_11_chamber_music_2.pdf, p. xxxix. Burial at Vestre Kirkegård: Dansk Biografisk Leksikon, “Carl Nielsen”, https://biografiskleksikon.lex.dk/Carl_Nielsen

fields.label: Performers
fields.value: Det Kgl. Kapels Blæserkvintet (Wind Quintet of the Royal Orchestra, Copenhagen) (ensemble), Holger Gilbert-Jespersen (flute), Svend Christian Felumb (oboe and cor anglais), Aage Oxenvad (clarinet), Hans Sørensen (horn), Knud Lassen (bassoon)
fields.note: The labels read “Det Kgl. Kapels Blæserkvintet. Gilbert Jespersen—Fløjte, Felumb—Oboe, Oxenvad—Klarinet, Kn. Lassen—Fagot & Hans Sørensen—Horn”. The Kelly files give the ensemble as the wind quintet of the Royal Orchestra, Copenhagen, with the same five names and Holger Gilbert-Jespersen in full. The item description calls the ensemble the Wind Quintet of the Royal Danish Opera and says Gilbert-Jespersen joined in 1929; the Catalogue of Carl Nielsen’s Works lists him as the flautist at the Berlin performance of 29 March 1923, and Paul Hagemann as flautist at the first public performance on 9 October 1922. The other four players are those named for that first performance.

fields.label: Work version
fields.value: Original version for flute, oboe (cor anglais in the Prelude and the theme), clarinet in A, horn in F and bassoon. The Prelude, the theme, all eleven variations and the closing Andantino festivo are present.
fields.note: The scoring is that of the score in the Carl Nielsen Edition. That nothing is cut was established by comparing the structure of the track (pauses at the printed fermatas, variation lengths in bars) with the printed bars, not by comparison with a published list of the sides. The labels read “3 Sats: Præludium–Tema con variazioni”, parts 1 to 4; which score edition the players used is not stated.

fields.label: Recorded
fields.note: The item description gives 24 January 1936, and the Kelly files date matrices 2CS 291–294 to that day. The first movement (matrices 296–297) was recorded on 25 January, and the Menuet side was remade as take 4 on 5 May 1936; neither is part of this track.

fields.label: Place
fields.note: The item description says “in Copenhagen, Denmark”, and the Kelly files give “Royal Orchestra, Copenhagen” as the ensemble. The place field in the Kelly files reads “Someplace, Scandanavia”, a placeholder. The studio or hall is not stated.

fields.label: Label
fields.value: His Master’s Voice (The Gramophone Company, Ltd.), 12-inch records in the Scandinavian red-label D.B. series, pressed in England
fields.note: The label scans read “His Master’s Voice”, “Made in England” and “The Gramophone Co. Ltd.”, in Danish, with “Quintett” and the speed, 78. The item description calls DB 5200–5203 the first issue in the 12-inch Scandinavian Red Label series.

fields.label: Catalogue
fields.value: HMV D.B. 5201 (side B), D.B. 5202 (sides A and B) and D.B. 5203 (side A), parts 1 to 4 of the third movement; the set is D.B. 5200–5203, 12-inch, 78 rpm
fields.note: Read from the label scans of D.B. 5201 B (“1 Del”), D.B. 5202 A (“2 Del”), D.B. 5202 B (“3 Del”) and D.B. 5203 A (“4 Del”). The Musical Quarterly of April 1937 lists the set as DB 5200–3, and The New Records of August 1937 as four 12-inch discs, DB5200 to DB5203. Side B of D.B. 5203 carries the Taagen letter from Nielsen’s music for Moderen.

fields.label: Matrix, take, sides
fields.note: The labels print the matrix numbers 2CS 294, 291, 292 and 293 without takes; the takes come from the item description and agree with the issued takes in the Kelly files. The set was numbered as one sequence of sides, and the labels carry the hand-marked side numbers 4 to 7.

fields.label: Transfer
fields.value: Internet Archive collection The Shellackophile’s Vintage Recordings; the person who made the transfer is not named in the item
fields.note: The item belongs to the collection described as recordings of classical music from the 78-rpm era. Photographs of the labels are included in the item; their photographer is not named.

fields.label: Transfer date
fields.value: Not stated; the item was made public on 17 March 2022
fields.note: The public date of the item and the modification time of the uploaded FLAC file are the same day, which is an upload date and not a transfer date.

fields.label: Processing
fields.value: The four sides of the movement are joined in one track of 13 min 22 s. Equalisation, noise reduction and speed correction are not described.
fields.note: The item has one track for the whole movement, and the surface noise changes at about 3:22, 7:19 and 11:00, which are the joins between sides 4 and 5, 5 and 6, and 6 and 7.

fields.label: Composition rights
fields.value: Public domain. Nielsen died on 3 October 1931, so the work has been out of copyright in the European Union (life plus 70 years) since the end of 2001. The first edition was published by Wilhelm Hansen, Copenhagen, in 1923, which makes it public domain in the United States as well.
fields.note: The dates are documented; the legal conclusion is ours. The Carl Nielsen Edition of 2003, used here only for bar numbers and the preface, is a separate publication under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 3.0 licence, and none of its text or music is reproduced.

fields.label: Recording rights
fields.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
fields.note: The set was listed as Danish Gramophone DB 5200–3 in The Musical Quarterly of April 1937 and reviewed as four 12-inch discs in The New Records of August 1937, so it was published by then. The uploader’s date of 1936 is not an independent source. The United States status of a Danish recording published in 1936 or 1937 is not established.

composer.born: 9 June 1865, Sortelung, Nørre Lyndelse, Funen, Denmark
composer.epithet: Danish composer, violinist and conductor, born on Funen and based in Copenhagen, who wrote six symphonies, the opera Maskarade, a wind quintet and a large body of songs and hymn tunes.
facts: Military bandsman in Odense, 1879–83 · Copenhagen Conservatory, 1884–86 (violin with Valdemar Tofte, theory with Orla Rosenhoff)
Second violin in the Royal Orchestra, 1889–1905 · conductor at the Royal Theatre, 1908–14 · conductor of the Music Society from 1915 · director of the Royal Danish Academy of Music from 1931
Symphony No. 1, 1894 · Maskarade, 1906 · Symphony No. 4, 1916 · Symphony No. 5 and the Wind Quintet, 1922
Six symphonies, two operas, concertos for violin, flute and clarinet, chamber and organ music, cantatas, and songs and hymn tunes for voice and choir

quote.text: The point is to be able to say a pure fifth in such a way that no one thinks he has heard that interval before.
quote.source: Carl Nielsen, quoted in the Dansk Biografisk Leksikon, “Carl Nielsen”; the occasion is not given there

composer.background:
Carl August Nielsen was born on 9 June 1865 at Sortelung, a cottage in the parish of Nørre Lyndelse on Funen. He was the seventh of twelve children. His father, Niels Jørgensen, was a house painter who played the fiddle at dances; he was known as Painter-Niels, and the children took Nielsen as their surname. At six, when he had measles, Carl was handed a three-quarter-size violin that hung on the wall, taught himself a few melodies and played them for his father. Emil Petersen, the assistant teacher at the village school, taught him to play from notes. Petersen later told how he had once passed Painter-Niels’s house and found a boy of seven or eight hammering on blocks of wood laid out as a keyboard.

Confirmed at fourteen, Nielsen was apprenticed to a shopkeeper whose business failed, and on 1 November 1879 he joined the band of the Sixteenth Battalion in Odense. In 1883 he showed a string quartet to Niels W. Gade in Copenhagen, and in January 1884 he entered the Conservatory on a scholarship, studying the violin and, with Orla Rosenhoff, theory and counterpoint. He left at the end of 1886. His Suite for Strings, Op. 1, was played at Tivoli on 8 September 1888, and in 1889 he joined the second violins of the Royal Orchestra, where he stayed for sixteen years.
